newsitem.title: SWEDEN: INTERVIEW - Thai Airways embarks on own cargo unit.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Thai Airways embarks on own cargo unit.

text.p: Thai Airways International Ltd said on Friday it was embarking on its own cargo business with the first step to lease a Boeing 747-200 freighter to fly under Thai colours on an existing Frankfurt-Bangkok route.
The state-owned airline, which has a cargo partnership with Lufthansa Cargo AG, also aimed to form a cargo division separate from its passenger division in the near future.

"It would be a big step into cargo but it's not unknown to us due to the Lufthansa cooperation," Thai Airways Scandinavia and Finland cargo sales manager Peter Sull told Reuters by telephone from Denmark.
"As soon as possible we'd like to start a jumbo freighter to Frankfurt and Los Angeles and a DC-10 for a regional operation."
Sull said the aircraft, to be leased from Atlas Air, would take over one of two weekly flights that Thai Airways currently operates with Lufthansa Cargo with a Lufthansa Boeing 747-200F.
Sull said it would probably start in October or November this year.
"We have signed a leasing contract already," Sull said.
Sull said Thai Airways and Lufthansa hoped to move to a daily service between Frankfurt and Bangkok when the market could handle increased capacity.
But proposals earlier this year to start a third freighter service each week this winter had been put on hold.
"We feel the market is too slow to add frequencies at the moment," Sull said.
"The future plan is to operate daily a Boeing 747 freighter between Frankfurt and Bangkok in cooperation with Lufthansa."
Sull said the airlines hoped to add a third flight in late 1997.
Sull said the airline planned to acquire another DC-10 freighter to put into operation for regional service to Singapore, Penang, Hong Kong, Taipei and possibly Shanghai.
It also planned to acquire, through leasing or buying, several other freighters for its fleet which currently consists only of passenger aircraft.
"In the near future, within three to five years, we should go up to five freighter aircraft," Sull said.
The Bangkok-based carrier plans to separate its cargo operations from its passenger airline, Sull said.
"The plan is to separate the Thai cargo from Thai Airways so it would be a separate unit and profit centre," he said.
Sull said Thai Airways planned to increase cargo terminal capacity at its Bangkok hub.
"An additional 27,000 square metres should be in operation by mid-1997. That would bring the Bangkok airport up to a handling capacity of 1.3 million tonnes a year," Sull said.
Thai Airways was also seeking to improve its operations by streamlining its handling operations and using bar coding, electronic booking and electronically transmitted airway bills.
Thai Airways moved about 650,000 tonnes of cargo in 1995 through Bangkok, of which about 475 tonnes a month was flown on passenger flights from Scandinavia or trucked to Frankfurt.
Thai Airways entered a code-sharing deal with Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) earlier this year and the two airlines operate 14 joint flights a week out of Denmark and Sweden.
